neighbours.label: the word that opens a frozen collocation whose continuation is fully predictable ('for all intents' → and purposes, 'halcyon' → days, 'beck' → and call)
fire: By the end of the summer the old factory was, for all intents and purposes, closed.
My grandmother still talks about the halcyon days before the war.
The merger is, to all intents and purposes, a simple takeover.
Fans remember the halcyon years of the club in the seventies.
After the scandal the minister was, for all intents and purposes, finished.
The assistant was at his beck and call from morning until night.
Those were the halcyon summers we spent on the lake.
The villagers raised a hue and cry when the bridge was closed.
quiet: By the end of the summer the old factory was, in practical terms, closed.
My grandmother still talks about the peaceful days before the war.
The merger is, in most respects, a simple takeover.
Fans remember the successful years of the club in the seventies.
After the scandal the minister was, in effect, finished.
The assistant was available to him from morning until night.
Those were the quiet summers we spent on the lake.
The villagers complained loudly when the bridge was closed.

notes: Card: halcy[on] days, all [intents] and purposes, Sense and Sens[ibility], take to the [skies]. Probe: intents 0.50, halcyon 0.44; 'cat out of the bag' 0.05, 'new crop of' 0.10, literal control 0.04. Near misses paraphrase the same content without the frozen phrase.
